subject: physics
question_text: What is graphene, and what makes it a super material?

mark_split.label: Why it is a super material

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 10 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: graphene is a single-atom-thick two-dimensional carbon lattice, about 200 times stronger than steel for its weight; the study material's own comparison that graphene is a million times thinner than a human hair is a loose figure, closer to 200,000 times by the true dimensions, so it was deliberately not repeated here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
lines: Graphene is a single layer of carbon
steps.why: Graphene is carbon arranged as flat, connected hexagons only one atom thick, which is what gives it such unusual strength and conductivity.
common_mistakes: Describing graphene as a three-dimensional crystal instead of a single flat layer.
Confusing graphene with graphite, which is many such layers stacked together.
steps.memory_tip: Graphene: one layer, one atom thick, carbon atoms in hexagons.
steps.margin_note: The words single layer or one atom thick must appear in this step.

steps.label: Why it is a super material
lines: very well, and is flexible and
steps.why: These properties together — strength for its weight, high heat and electrical conductivity, flexibility and near transparency — are why graphene is called a super material.
common_mistakes: Writing that graphene is a million times thinner than a human hair — that printed comparison is inaccurate; write one atom thick instead.
Naming only one property instead of at least two.
steps.memory_tip: Remember: one atom thick, about 200 times stronger than steel by weight.
steps.margin_note: Do not write a million times thinner than a hair; write one atom thick.
